history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: several Hanuman temples exist in Shillong (e.g. the Garikhana Hanuman Temple on G S Road and the Shri Hanuman Mandir on NH 40 near Upper Mawprem, both with Justdial listings), so the generic CSV name is ambiguous. The best-supported referent used here is the Shree Shree Hanuman Mandir of the Jaiaw/Garikhana area - geocoded at Hanuman Temple, Luckier Road, Lower Mawprem, Garikhana, Shillong 793002 (full-address match; consistent with Meta place data 25.578403, 91.873244), documented in detail by inheritage.foundation. Per inheritage: a hilltop temple built by the local Hindu community during the British colonial period (Shillong became the capital of Assam in 1874, drawing Hindu government servants and traders who built the temple as a community anchor); a predominantly white structure with red/orange Hanuman colours and a sloping roof adapted to the heavy rainfall; a towering orange Hanuman idol in the sanctum plus a smaller Shiva shrine; panoramic views over Shillong; and a role as a community centre hosting festivals and social gatherings, attracting devotees across faiths. A May 2026 news report describes miscreants vandalising a Hanuman temple in Shillong's Garikhana locality (idols of Krishna-Radha and Hanuman, silver ornaments and cash stolen; FIR by Ravi Sharma; Lumdiengjri police station) - plausibly this same Garikhana shrine (verify). Flag: identity uncertain - field verification needed to confirm which Shillong Hanuman shrine the CSV row intends.

name: Hanuman Temple, Shillong
town_description: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya in the East Khasi Hills district, a hill station at about 1,496 m known as the 'Scotland of the East'. It was the capital of undivided Assam until 1972 and remains the state's administrative, educational and cultural hub, with a predominantly Khasi tribal population alongside Bengali, Nepali, Assamese and other communities (verify). The primary referent used here lies in the Jaiaw/Garikhana area (Luckier Road, Lower Mawprem), southwest of central Shillong (verify).

travel.airport: Shillong (Umroi) Airport, approx. 25-30 km from the city (verify; limited scheduled services). Nearest major airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 100-125 km by road; verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 100 km by road; verify); onward by taxi or bus via NH-6.
travel.road: Shillong is well connected by road to Guwahati (approx. 3-4 hours via NH-6; verify); within the city, local taxis and shared cabs serve all localities (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather (10-20°C, per inheritage), avoiding the monsoon. Hanuman Jayanti (March-April) is the most vibrant time to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-1:00 PM & 4:00 PM-8:00 PM daily, per inheritage (verify - temple-managed hours not independently confirmed). Entry free per inheritage (verify). Early morning (6-9 AM) or evening (4-7 PM) recommended for aarti; dress modestly.
